articles.title: Simultaneous imaging of arterial and venous territories in human cutaneous microcirculation: An ex vivo anatomical model.
articles.authors: Martin Lhuaire, Aïna Venkatasamy, Severine Carrion et al.
articles.abstract: Accurate visualisation of the arterial and venous components of the cutaneous microcirculation remains essential for understanding perforator flap anatomy and skin vascular organisation. Although traditional vascular injection techniques provide detailed anatomical information, their compatibility with modern multimodal imaging and simultaneous arteriovenous radiological discrimination remains limited. This study developed and performed a proof-of-concept evaluation of an ex vivo imaging model for radiological discrimination of selectively injected arterial and venous vascular compartments using dual-dilution latex-barium sulphate (BaSO4) co-injection combined with mammography and photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT). An initial in vitro calibration using a tubing phantom was performed to determine optimal contrast dilutions. The protocol was subsequently evaluated using thigh perforator flaps obtained from 21 fresh-frozen human donors. Eighteen donors underwent combined arterial and venous injections using red arterial (1/2) and blue venous (1/10) latex-BaSO4 mixtures, while three additional donors underwent venous-only injections. Specimens were analysed using magnified mammography and PCCT. Quantitative assessment included signal intensity, signal-to-noise ratio and contrast-to-noise ratio. In vitro experiments demonstrated a linear relationship between contrast concentration and signal intensity, with maximal arteriovenous radiological discrimination obtained using 1/2 and 1/10 dilutions. Mammography provided consistent discrimination between arterial and venous compartments across submillimetre vessel diameters. PCCT enabled three-dimensional visualisation of the vascular network but showed greater variability in radiological discrimination between the predefined arterial and venous compartments, mainly due to voxel size limitations and partial-volume averaging. Incomplete venous filling represented the principal technical limitation and reduced the proportion of specimens suitable for dual-compartment analysis. Completeness of capillary filling was not independently validated. This proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of simultaneous imaging of selectively injected arterial and venous vascular compartments within the same human specimen. Magnified mammography enabled reliable radiological differentiation between compartments, whereas current PCCT settings were insufficient for equivalent separation. Further optimisation of venous perfusion and independent validation of distal microvascular filling are required before broader quantitative anatomical application.

articles.title: Classification of hyperplastic anterior choroidal arteries: arterial distribution and proposed sites of persistent anastomosis.
Deep learning classification of children with autism spectrum disorder using short-duration center of pressure data.
articles.authors: Yumeng Li, Maya Nachega, Sugru Yahaya et al.
articles.abstract: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often demonstrate impaired postural stability. However, assessment of postural stability in this population can be challenging because prolonged standing trials may increase spontaneous fidgeting and reduce data quality. Convolutional neural network (CNN) may offer a practical approach for identifying ASD-related postural control patterns using short-duration center of pressure (COP) data. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the classification performance of a CNN for distinguishing children with ASD from healthy controls using short duration COP data. 49 children, including 20 typically developing children and 29 children with ASD, completed quiet-standing trials on a force plate. COP data were analyzed using CNN models trained separately with 5 s, 10 s, and 15 s COP data inputs. Classification accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score were calculated to assess the model performance. In general, classification performance improved as COP input duration increased. Using 5 s COP data, the CNN model achieved a classification accuracy of 77.6 %. When the duration was increased to 10 s, accuracy improved substantially to 96.7 %. Extending the duration to 15 s resulted in a minor increase in accuracy to 98.8 %. These findings indicate that short-duration COP contains discriminative information in this sample. Larger multisite samples and external validation are required before clinical application.

articles.title: Automated action potential parameter analysis for reproducible electrophysiological measurements in neurons.
articles.authors: Dmytro V Vasylyev, Stephen G Waxman
articles.abstract: Quantitative analysis of action potential (AP) waveforms is central to studies of neuronal excitability, ion channel function, disease mechanisms and pharmacological modulation. However, AP analysis is still often performed using partially manual workflows or proprietary software environments that can constrain the amount of information extracted from APs and limit reproducibility, transparency and throughput. Here, we present a freely available, open-source software tool for extracting AP parameters, developed for use with the OriginLab software package Origin/OriginPro. APpar detects APs from membrane voltage recordings using a user-defined derivative criterion and calculates a comprehensive set of excitability parameters, including resting membrane potential, voltage threshold, overshoot, afterhyperpolarization (AHP), AP amplitude, rise and decay time, AP duration, AP half-width, AP width at 0 mV, AP area above voltage threshold, dV/dtmax, dV/dtmin and interspike interval for the respective AP. Because AP threshold is a particularly sensitive and method-dependent measurement, APpar includes a TRUE-threshold validation algorithm. After the initial forward dV/dt threshold crossing is identified, the software finds AP overshoot, searches backward to the closest preceding local dV/dt maximum, then searches backward to the user-defined dV/dt crossing and recalculates AP parameters from this validated threshold point. We validated APpar using APs from dorsal root ganglion neuron current-clamp recordings, including copied identical APs, current-evoked repetitive firing and long-duration spontaneous firing. The software produced stable measurements from identical copied APs and extracted dynamic changes in AP parameters across repetitive and spontaneous firing sequences. APpar provides a transparent, customizable and Origin-compatible framework for reproducible AP analysis in neuronal electrophysiology. KEY POINTS: Action potential (AP) waveforms contain important information about neuronal excitability and function of the underlying ion channels, but their analysis is often performed using partially manual, labour-intensive workflows, constraining the amount of information extracted from each AP, which can limit reproducibility and throughput. Measurements such as AP threshold, amplitude and duration depend strongly on how threshold is defined, creating variability between studies and laboratories. We developed APpar, a freely available open-source software tool that automatically detects APs and extracts a comprehensive set of waveform and excitability parameters within the widely used Origin/OriginPro environment. APpar incorporates a novel TRUE-threshold (Temporally Reversed Unsupervised Extraction of the Threshold) validation algorithm that improves the consistency of derivative-based threshold detection while preserving user control over physiologically meaningful analysis settings. Validation using dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neuron recordings showed that APpar provides stable measurements and enables efficient analysis of single AP, repetitive and spontaneous firing, supporting reproducible studies of neuronal excitability and ion channel function.

articles.title: DEL-1 deficiency exacerbates inflammation-driven cardiac dysfunction during angiotensin II-induced hypertension.
articles.authors: Alina Maslakova, Maria Knyrim, Michael Marterstock et al.
articles.abstract: Hypertension is associated with inflammatory activation in the heart that contributes to cardiac remodelling and functional impairment, yet the mechanisms that regulate these cardiac inflammatory responses remain incompletely understood. Developmental endothelial locus-1 (DEL-1) is a secreted immunomodulatory glycoprotein that regulates leukocyte recruitment and inflammation resolution; however, its constitutive role in cardiac inflammation and remodelling during hypertension has not been defined. Here, we investigated the function of DEL-1 during angiotensin II (ANGII)-induced hypertension using Del1-deficient mice. Echocardiographic analysis revealed a distinct temporal pattern of cardiac remodelling during ANGII infusion. Del1KO mice developed early systolic dysfunction accompanied by diastolic alterations three days after ANGII infusion, whereas wild-type (WT) littermates maintained preserved systolic performance at this stage. Importantly, these functional differences occurred in the absence of differences in arterial pressure, suggesting a blood pressure independent mechanism. Flow cytometric analysis demonstrated markedly enhanced recruitment of neutrophils and inflammatory Ly6Chi monocytes into Del1KO hearts during the early phase of hypertension, indicating amplified inflammatory activation. This was accompanied by activation of the bone marrow haematopoietic compartment, characterized by an early expansion of long-term haematopoietic stem cells, followed by a transient increase in haematopoietic progenitor populations during the intermediate phase of hypertension. During later stages of hypertension, systolic function partially recovered in Del1KO mice but was accompanied by exaggerated hypertrophic remodelling and increased cardiac fibrosis. Together, these findings identify DEL-1 as an endogenous regulator that restrains early cardiac inflammation at the onset of hypertension and supports balanced cardiac adaptation during prolonged hypertensive stress. KEY POINTS: Hypertension is associated with cardiac inflammation and remodelling, but endogenous mechanisms that restrain early inflammatory cardiac injury remain incompletely defined. Developmental endothelial locus-1 (DEL-1) deficiency caused early systolic dysfunction and diastolic alterations during angiotensin II-induced hypertension, despite no early difference in arterial blood pressure. Loss of DEL-1 amplified early recruitment of neutrophils and Ly6Chi inflammatory monocytes to the heart and was associated with activation of the bone marrow haematopoietic compartment. At later stages, systolic function partially recovered in Del1KO mice, but this was accompanied by exaggerated fibrotic remodelling and increased profibrotic gene expression. These findings identify endogenous DEL-1 as a protective regulator that limits early inflammatory cardiac injury and supports balanced cardiac adaptation during hypertensive stress.

The Development of the Strength and Conditioning Coach Evaluation Tool.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: David LaPlaca, Paul Schempp, Jeremy Elliott et al.
articles.abstract: LaPlaca, D, Schempp, P, Elliott, J, Weldon, A, and Bishop, C. The development of the strength and conditioning coach evaluation tool. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to develop a tool to assess the level of coaching skills of strength and conditioning (S&C) coaches. The study involved 213 S&C coaches working on the elite level with an average of 13.8 years of experience, employed across Major League Baseball, Major League Soccer, National Basketball Association, National Football League, National Hockey League, Armed Forces, Australian Football League, English Premier League, and NCAA Division 1 FBS "Power Five" Conferences. Subjects completed an evaluation form composed of qualitative and quantitative questions. Hereafter, 22 subjects further completed a test-retest within 2 weeks, the intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.771 (95% confidence interval: 0729-0.807), demonstrating statistical reliability. This study has produced a preliminary evaluation tool that is reliable for evaluating S&C coaching expertise. It can be used by S&C coaches, their supervisors, and non-S&C managers to guide professional development and assesses the current skills, knowledge, and experiences of a S&C coach.

articles.title: Citrulline Malate Ingestion Enhances Muscular Performance During a Selected Hypertrophy Hack Squat Training Protocol.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Benjamin Wax, Sandor Dorgo, Samuel Montalvo et al.
articles.abstract: Wax, B, Dorgo, S, Montalvo, S, Lyons, B, and Mayo, JJ. Citrulline malate ingestion enhances muscular performance during a selected hypertrophy hack squat training protocol. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study examined potential ergogenic effects of an oral citrulline malate supplement (CM) during lower-body resistance training. Fifteen resistance-trained men completed a randomized, counterbalanced, double-blind crossover design. Subjects ingested 8.0 g CM or placebo 60 minutes before 8 sets of hack squats at 67% one-repetition maximum to failure with 90-second recovery intervals, repeating the protocol with the alternate treatment 1 week later. Blood lactate before and after exercise, rating of perceived exertion after sets 4 and 8, muscle soreness at 24 and 48 hours, and heart rate and blood pressure at rest and 5 and 10 minutes after exercise were assessed. Hack squat repetition numbers were higher overall in the CM condition (condition effect p = 0.0213), and CM increased total repetitions by 10.7 (95% confidence interval 1.4 to 20.0; p = 0.0265; Hedges' g = 0.61) and total workload by 1,064.7 units (95% confidence interval 84.1 to 2045.4; p = 0.0354; Hedges' g = 0.57). Blood lactate increased after exercise but did not differ by condition. Rating of perceived exertion showed no significant condition effect or Holm-adjusted set-specific difference. Citrulline malate was associated with significantly lower muscle soreness overall and at both 24 and 48 hours after exercise. Heart rate and systolic blood pressure showed condition × time interactions, with Holm-adjusted CM vs. placebo differences at 5 minutes after exercise, whereas diastolic blood pressure showed no significant condition effect or Holm-adjusted time-point difference. Acute CM supplementation may improve lower-body resistance training work capacity and reduce perceived soreness without altering lactate accumulation or perceived exertion.

articles.title: Postactivation Performance Enhancement in Highly Trained Sprinters: Effects of Different Jump Squat Loading Strategies.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Túlio B M A Moura, Lucas A Pereira, Tomás T Freitas et al.
articles.abstract: Moura, TBMA, Pereira, LA, Freitas, TT, Mercer, VP, Moura, FA, and Loturco, I. Postactivation performance enhancement in highly trained sprinters: Effects of different jump squat loading strategies. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to investigate the acute effects of different conditioning activities (CAs) on sprint and jump performance, and on muscle contractile properties, in highly trained sprinters. Thirteen male athletes participated in this randomized crossover study. Countermovement jump (CMJ) height, 50-m sprint performance, and muscle contractile properties assessed via tensiomyography (TMG) were measured before and at 5 and 10 minutes after the execution of 1 set of 3 jump squat (JS) repetitions performed either at the optimum power load (JS OPL) or at 80% of 1 repetition maximum (JS 80% 1RM) in a crossover design. Generalized estimating equations were used to analyze the effect of the different CAs on CMJ and sprint performance, whereas a 2-way ANOVA was conducted to analyze the effect of the CAs on the TMG-derived variables. Individual performance responses were examined using the "true change" approach. No significant changes were observed after both JS OPL and JS 80% 1RM protocols in CMJ height, sprint performance, or TMG-derived variables (p > 0.05). Overall, the execution of JS-based CAs did not elicit consistent performance enhancements when conventional group-level analyses were applied. Considering the small performance variations typically observed in sprinters, practitioners are advised to use individualized monitoring and more sensitive analytical approaches to better identify meaningful performance changes when using acute performance enhancement strategies.

articles.title: Effects of succinate supplements on metabolic health and muscle mass after mechanical overloading and denervation of skeletal muscles in mice fed high-fat or ketogenic diet.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Mantas Dirmontas, Petras Minderis, Aivaras Ratkevicius
articles.abstract: Succinate might mediate muscle exercise-induced adaptations in body tissues and organs. We studied metabolic health and body composition in 6-month-old C57BL/6J mouse males after 12 weeks of feeding regular diet (RD, kcal distribution: 13% fat, 57% carbohydrate, 30% protein), high-fat diet (HFD, kcal distribution: 60% fat, 20% carbohydrates, 20% protein) or ketogenic diet (KD, kcal distribution: 80% fat, < 1% carbohydrates, 20% protein) with or without 2% succinate supplements (SUS) in drinking water (n = 10 in each group). In additional set of experiments, functional overloading (FO) of the plantaris muscle (PL) was induced in a group of mice by denervation of the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles at week 6 for all six dietary intervention groups (n = 8-10 in each group). HFD induced the greatest (p < 0.001) increase in body and fat mass. SUS blunted (p < 0.01) initial surge in energy intake when mice were switched to HFD, but did not influence metabolic health measures at the end of study.Mechanical overloading induced ~25% increase in PL mass which was not affected by diet or SUS. In conclusion, SUS does not have a long-term effect on metabolic health or skeletal muscle hypertrophy after overloading.

articles.title: Protection by ascorbate and catechin at high physiological concentrations against myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in an isolated rat heart model.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Ahmed Abou Hadeed, Kosar Omidian, Hossein Rafiei et al.
articles.abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is an important health concern in myocardial infarction and situations such as angioplasty and cardiac surgeries. Ascorbate (vitamin C) and flavonoids such as catechin are known for their antioxidant activity and are of interest as supplements or added to perfused blood during surgeries to limit I/R injury. While intravenous ascorbate during surgeries has been studied in clinical trials, it has usually been at high pharmacological concentrations (with potential unwanted prooxidant activity). The objectives of this study were to 1) determine the extent to which ascorbate or catechin alone, added to the perfusate at levels which could be in blood after dietary supplementation, can protect myocardial tissue in the reperfusion phase of I/R injury, and 2) evaluate the possible cooperative or synergistic protective effect of ascorbate and catechin when given together. Isolated rat hearts (n=48) were perfused in the retrograde mode with modified Krebs-Henseleit buffer, and following the induction of 30 min global ischemia, ascorbate (150 μM) and/or catechin (5 μM) were added directly into the perfusate during 90 min reperfusion. The experiments showed that 150 μM ascorbate protected the heart against lipid peroxidation and cell apoptosis by 100%, while 5 μM catechin protected by 67% and 90% respectively. Due to the strong protection by ascorbate alone, no cooperative protective effect could be observed when ascorbate and catechin were used together. In conclusion, this preclinical study showed strong protection against myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury by ascorbate in the perfusate at a much lower concentration than most clinical trials, and protection by catechin at a physiological dose.

articles.title: Longitudinal Associations of Hip Flexor Size and Strength with Physical Function in Older Adults with Chronic Low Back Pain.
articles.authors: Felix Marechal, J Megan Sions, Ryan T Pohlig et al.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Older adults with chronic low back pain (cLBP) experience greater functional decline than their pain-free peers, which increases their mortality risk. OBJECTIVE: The objective was to investigate the contribution of hip flexor size into future physical function, beyond hip flexion strength, among older adults with cLBP. DESIGN: This was a 12-month longitudinal study. SETTING: This study was conducted in a clinical research laboratory. PARTICIPANTS: The sample included 250 community-dwelling older adults with cLBP. EXPOSURE(S): Hip flexion strength was measured at baseline via hand-held dynamometry. Hip flexor cross-sectional area (CSA) was measured at baseline for the iliopsoas, rectus femoris, and sartorius via ultrasound brightness mode. To avoid multicollinearity between CSA measures, the hip flexor CSA with the strongest bivariate correlation with the outcome measures was used for analyses. MAIN OUTCOME(S) AND MEASURE(S): Physical function was captured through the 6-Minute Walk Test and the Stair Climb Test, at baseline and 12-month follow-up. RESULTS: At 12 months, 6-Minute Walk Test performance was explained by baseline hip flexion strength (b = 2.439, SE = 1.034, η2p = 0.030), but not by baseline hip flexor CSA. Conversely, Stair Climb Test performance was not explained by baseline hip flexion strength but was explained by baseline hip flexor CSA (b = -0.258, SE = 0.121, η2p = 0.027). CONCLUSIONS: Hip flexion strength and hip flexor size provide distinct insights into future physical function among older adults with cLBP. Hip flexion strength is longitudinally associated with walking capacity, whereas hip flexor CSA provides insight into stairs performance. RELEVANCE: Rehabilitation professionals may consider capturing both hip flexion strength and hip flexor size to better represent ambulatory needs of older adults with cLBP. These modifiable hip characteristics may also help clinicians tailor interventions to their patients' rehabilitation goals.
